title: Infix DSL-Style Syntax

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Infix DSL-Style Syntax** as part of **Functional Programming and Idiomatic Kotlin**. Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions. Use the subtopics—Infix Function Requirements, Readable Domain Expressions, Avoiding Ambiguous APIs—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with infix function requirements. Then compare it with readable domain expressions. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Infix Function Requirements
items.text: Infix Function Requirements describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Readable Domain Expressions
items.text: Readable Domain Expressions should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Avoiding Ambiguous APIs
items.text: Avoiding Ambiguous APIs crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

fun multiply(value: Int, factor: Int = 2): Int = value * factor

fun main() = println(multiply(6))
